title: Vilasa 6. Gauranga in Kheturi and the Gathering of the Vaishnavas for the Festival
html:
Narottama in Kheturi: in a dream the Lord reveals His Deity in a granary; the beginning of the kirtana; news of Srinivasa (his marriage, Ramachandra, his second journey to Vrindavana); the meeting at Budhari; the invitations and the coming of the Vaishnavas, led by Jahnava

1Glory to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with their associates!
Be merciful, Prabhu, to this wretched beggar.

2Glory, glory to the listeners, oceans of mercy!
Hear what I shall now relate.

3Having crossed the river Padmavati, the Mahashaya
entered the village of Sri Kheturi at an auspicious moment.

4People came from all sides and gazed their fill;
Kheturi was immersed in an ocean of bliss.

5Sri Santosha and others carefully took
Sri Thakura Mahashaya to a very secluded dwelling.

6Still there was no end to the coming and going of people;
the crowd stayed day and night, into the late watches.

7Sri Thakura Mahashaya, at night, in seclusion,
thought: "How shall I manifest the service?"

8At the end of the night sleep drew him in,
and in a dream the son of Shachi said:

9"O Narottama, watching the road for you,
I have long been present in a metal Deity.

10In your kingdom there is a prominent householder;
everyone knows him as a very wealthy man.

11In his house are many granaries for grain,
but no one can go there for fear of a huge snake.

12In the biggest of them am I:
open the door and bring Me quickly."

13Having spoken also of the making of other Deities,
He embraced Narottama and vanished.

14In separation from the dream Sri Thakura Mahashaya
awoke in agitation and saw that six dandas of night remained.

15Passing the rest of the night in chanting the holy name,
he quickly cleaned his teeth and bathed.

16With great joy he asked everyone:
"Where is there a householder with a large family,

17who has many granaries for grain,
where no one can go for fear of a snake?"

18All said, "We know him."
The Thakura said, "Then let us go.

19I have a very secret purpose there."
Saying this, the Mahashaya set out.

20He went quickly to that householder's house,
and he with his whole family deemed himself blessed.

21As Sri Thakura Mahashaya went toward the granary,
the householder anxiously fell at his feet,

22and with joined palms said, weeping:
"Everyone knows there is danger there from a huge snake.

23Many snake-charmers came to drive the snake away,
but at the snake's hissing none could stand firm.

24We abandoned it long ago;
there are many valuable goods in it, and we grieve.

25Come what may, we will not let you go there;
whatever your business, we will do it here."

26Smiling, Sri Thakura Mahashaya said:
"Do not worry: the fear of the snake will go far away.

27In your granary is something greatly needed;
you will see it with your own eyes, and your eyes will be fulfilled."

28Saying this, the Thakura Mahashaya went on,
while all the people trembled with fear.

29At the sight of Sri Thakura Mahashaya's approach,
the huge snakes vanished.

30As Narottama, in prema, opened the door,
he saw the Moon of Navadvipa with His Beloved.1

31His body shone, adorned with ornaments —
nowhere could anything be found to compare.

32As he spread his arms to take Him up,
He flashed like lightning and entered his embrace.

33Seeing this, all the people were astonished,
crying "Jaya! Jaya!" with tears in their eyes.

34They said to one another, "We have seen a marvel:
such a deed is never possible for a man."

35Some said: "Others cannot recognize him;
by his mercy this land will be blessed."

36Some said: "If we are fortunate,
we shall surely take shelter of these feet."

37Crying "Glory, glory to Prabhu Narottama!"
all danced with arms upraised.

38As the Mahashaya carried Prabhu to his dwelling,
people ran from all sides; there was a great crowd on the road.

39Reaching his dwelling, he carefully seated
Gaurachandra with His Beloved on a wondrous seat.

40Gazing on that beauty with unblinking eyes,
he was overwhelmed and could not check his tears.

41Suddenly there arose in his heart
all that the science of music speaks of — dance, song and instruments.

42At once the Mahashaya, clapping his hands,
sang of Gaurachandra's virtues with his people.

43What wondrous singing the Mahashaya created!
At the sight of that dancing the pride of the gandharvas was destroyed.

44Thus in the Stavamrita-lahari:
To him who with his own dancing, destroying the pride of the gandharvas,
astonished all the people of the age of Kali,
who is renowned for the songs he himself created —
to Sri Narottama, obeisances, obeisances!2

45On whomever he casts a merciful glance but once,
he becomes a singer and in his singing showers prema.

46Even the lowest yavana, barbarian or evil-doer
sings, maddened, of Gauranga's pastimes.

47The sound of the kirtana rose and filled the world;
the gods from heaven showered flowers.

48Who could keep composure hearing that lofty singing?
What to speak of others — wood and stone split apart.

49The gandharvas and kinnaras said: "What a marvel!
Who has suddenly made such singing known?

50Such a mode of song is rare even in the world of the gods —
have dance, song and music themselves taken form?"

51Some said: "What is impossible for a devotee of Chaitanya?
Chaitanya's devotees are worshipped by all the gods."

52Saying this, they came in human guise
and fell at Narottama's feet, rolling on the ground.

53What happened — who could describe it?
After a while all were calmed with effort.

54That same day Balarama and many others
received the holy mantra from the Thakura.

55From that day the kirtana had its auspicious beginning;
the other festivities I cannot describe.

56Sri Thakura Mahashaya, with joy in his heart,
beheld Gaurachandra with Lakshmi and Vishnupriya.3

57Having appointed the brahmana Balarama and other disciples
to the service of the Deity of Gaura,

58and manifesting five more services by command in a dream,4
he was anxious, having no news of the Acharya.

59The Mahashaya pondered within himself:
"Without his permission how can I send a man?

60What shall I do now? Many days have passed,
and no one has come here from Yajigrama."

61As he pondered thus, growing anxious,
at that moment a man came from Yajigrama.

62Seeing him, Sri Thakura Mahashaya rejoiced,
seated him and asked after his welfare.

63He said: "All is well; I shall tell it in order.
In Yajigrama everyone is always anxious about you.

64He5 mostly stays in Shrikhanda and Kantaka-nagara,
and at times goes about the region of Navadvipa.

65One day Acharya Thakura went to Khanda,
and Sri Sarakara Thakura admonished him at length.

66Again taking his hand, he commanded again and again:
'My child, you must marry.'

67A command given again and again cannot be transgressed —
he married; hearing this, everyone rejoiced.

68Having married, he lives in Sri Yajigrama,
and many learned men come there to become disciples.

69A resident of Khanda, the son of Chiranjiva Sena,
named Ramachandra, expert in all the shastras —

70that he has made him his disciple" — on hearing this,
Narottama felt prema spontaneously arise in his heart.

71He went on: "Thus he has made many disciples
and spread the Gosvamis' books everywhere.

72He sent news to Vrindavana,
and a man came from there with a letter.

73The books that Sri Jiva Gosvami sent again
he quickly spread everywhere.

74A letter came from Navadvipa with news:
many devotees in Nadia have passed from sight.

75In Shantipura and other places the Lord's associates
have almost all passed away, burned by the fire of separation.

76At the passing of Sri Sarakara Thakura and Sri Dasa Gadadhara
the Acharya's heart was burned.

77The state the Acharya fell into cannot be told;
the life in the Acharya's body hung in doubt.

78Hearing his weeping, beasts and birds wept;
the Acharya could not restrain himself even for a moment.

79Without saying anything to anyone he left in the morning
and in a very short time entered Vrindavana.

80Seeing the Acharya, all the Gosvamis rejoiced,
sat with him in seclusion and asked after his welfare.

81How he took the books and how he spread them —
the Acharya told it all from beginning to end.

82When he told of the passing of the Lord's associates,
all, distraught, wept.

83Growing calm and understanding the Acharya's heart,
all spoke many words of consolation to the Acharya.

84As four or five days passed thus,
Ramachandra Sena came and joined them there.

85All learned about Ramachandra —
whose grandson and whose son he is.6

86He showed himself in Vraja as a great logician and poet,
and all the Gosvamis gave him the title 'Kaviraja.'

87How the Acharya had married
all heard from the Kaviraja.

88Sri Jiva Gosvami and the others, with great care,
sent him off, entrusting him with some books,

89and gave him four men of Vraja as companions.
The Acharya set out, weeping much.

90Sri Gopala Bhatta, Lokanatha and the others
were distraught, gazing at the road the Acharya had taken.

91The Thakura came back to Gauda very quickly
and, going to Vishnupura, set the king at ease.

92Hearing that he would come to Yajigrama,
I came alone with all the news."

93Even as he said this, another man came
and gave him a letter in Sri Acharya's own hand.

94Reading the letter, the Thakura Mahashaya
lost his composure, but still told the letter's meaning:

95"Sri Acharya, leaving his house with his people,
came to Kanchanagadiya and made two disciples:

96the brahmana Haridasa, foremost among the Lord's associates —
Shridasa and Gokulananda, his two sons —

97the two brothers became disciples at their father's bidding;
they are great panditas, intoxicated with the rasa of sankirtana.

98From there both have come with joy at heart:
Acharya Thakura came to Budhari yesterday."

99"Today is a blessed morning for me!" — saying this,
he went with the two to the temple of Sri Gaura

100and briefly told everything
to the pujari Balarama and all who were there.

101The pujari Balarama, with supreme joy at heart,
fed the two with Sri maha-prasada.

102Meanwhile the Mahashaya went to see
the storerooms prepared for the great festival.

103Seeing all ready, with gladness in his heart
he set each one to his task.

104Taking with him Devidasa, Gokula and Gauranga,7
he set out at dawn for the village of Budhari.

105As he entered the village, people, seeing him, rejoiced
and went quickly to tell Sri Acharya Thakura.

106Acharya Thakura, with great joy in his heart,
saw at the gate of the house that the Mahashaya had come.

107As the Mahashaya fell to the ground in obeisance,
the Acharya embraced him and could not be calm.

108The ocean of prema surged up immeasurably;
all who saw it were amazed.

109The Acharya himself introduced Sri Thakura Mahashaya
to Ramachandra and everyone else.

110What a meeting it was, full of the bliss of prema —
I have told something of it at length in the Bhakti-ratnakara.

111Acharya Thakura told Sri Thakura Mahashaya
all that had happened, in a secluded room:

112how he made Ramachandra and others his disciples,
how, after marrying, he went to Vraja,

113how Ramachandra and others went to Vrindavana,
how he received the title "Kaviraja,"

114how he came back to Gauda, to Vishnupura,
how he came from Yajigrama to Budhari,

115how the title "Kaviraja" was given to Govinda —
all this he told with joy in his heart.

116He asked Sri Thakura Mahashaya how things stood,
and the Mahashaya told everything in order:

117how Sri Santosha Raya and others became disciples,
how Bhakti-devi showed mercy to all,

118what festivity there was at the finding of Sri Gaura's Deity,
how the five other Deities were made,

119how the great festival was prepared,
how the holy temple and the throne were built.

120Having said this, he added: "As soon as I received the letter,
I set my mind on the festival at Phalguna-purnima."

121The Acharya said, "That day is settled,"
and, saying this, had letters of invitation written.

122Wherever devotees lived in Sri Gauda-mandala,
there letters of invitation were sent.

123He quickly sent a man to Utkala
and wrote all this to Shyamananda.

124Having joyfully sent letters everywhere,
he told the Mahashaya something in private — I do not know what.

125Overwhelmed by the relish of talks about Krishna,
he entrusted Narottama to Ramachandra.

126These two have one body, life and mind;
only to the eye are they two separate embodiments of prema.

127The ways of Sri Acharya, Narottama and Ramachandra
became known within a day or two.

128Some said: "These three are not human at all;
the three have appeared to deliver living beings."

129Some said: "O brother, looking at the three,
it seems to me that they are one substance in three."

130Some said: "What arises in my heart
I cannot reveal or tell to anyone."

131People said many such things to one another;
for fear of the book's length I cannot expand on them.

132The Acharya, keeping the Mahashaya four days,
sent him off to go ahead to Kheturi.

133He gave him as companions Ramachandra and other dear ones,
and arriving in Kheturi, all saw Gauranga.

134Shridasa and Gokulananda, treasuries of virtues,
Vyasa Acharya and others — all greatly learned —

135all rejoiced at heart
to see the great abundance for Prabhu's service.

136Sri Thakura Mahashaya together with Ramachandra
gave everyone lodgings, choosing secluded ones.

137Narottama, Ramachandra and all the others
watched the road for the Acharya.

138Meanwhile Sri Acharya, having made some more disciples,
came quickly to Kheturi with Govinda and others.

139What wondrous splendour there was as he entered the village!
All the Vaishnavas came out to receive him.

140The bliss of prema surged in everyone's heart;
they brought the Acharya to a wonderful lodging.

141From the lodging Acharya Thakura with his companions
went quickly to have darshan of Sri Gauranga.

142Seeing Gaura Raya with Lakshmi and Vishnupriya,
he was overwhelmed and bathed in tears.

143Seeing the five other Deities as well,
he entered such prema as cannot be described.

144After a while, growing calm, with his dear ones
he looked over all the provisions prepared in the house.

145Coming back to the lodging with his people, he kept saying:
"Why is Shyamananda so late in coming?"

146At that moment someone suddenly came and said:
"Shyamananda has come from Utkala."

147Hearing this, the Acharya rejoiced at heart,
and the Mahashaya went forward with his people.

148At that moment Shyamananda with his people
came and quickly entered the Acharya's house.

149Shyamananda, seeing the Acharya,
could not hold himself up; tears poured from his eyes.

150Acharya Thakura, out of affection, could not be calm
and embraced Shyamananda as he was bowing.

151He drenched Shyamananda with the tears of his eyes,
and all, seeing it, lost their composure in prema.

152The Acharya, gazing at Shyamananda's face,
asked after his welfare and after a while grew calm.

153What Narottama and Shyamananda were like in prema
cannot be told.

154Sri Thakura Mahashaya introduced
all the Vaishnavas to Sri Shyamananda:

155Shridasa, Gokulananda, Vyasa Chakravarti,
Ramachandra, Govinda and others bearing the title "Kaviraja."

156The joy of meeting Chattaraja, Ramakrishna, Kumuda and others8 —
who could describe it?

157Sri Shyamananda's disciples, Rasikananda and others,
Narottama, the treasury of virtues, brought together with all.

158The ways of love and devotion in their meeting —
whoever saw it deems himself virtuous.

159Narottama Mahashaya with Ramachandra
took Shyamananda to a wonderful lodging.

160Giving him lodging there, with great gladness of heart
he said affectionately to Rasikananda:

161"My child, you will see to everything,
so that no one is in any way slighted."

162Hearing this, Rasikananda, with joined palms,
deeming himself blessed, stood silent.

163Seeing Rasikananda's conduct, the Mahashaya
was more pleased than can be told.

164Sri Thakura Mahashaya together with Ramachandra
went to where Sri Acharya Thakura was.

165He sent Sri Govinda Kaviraja,
and he came gladly to Shyamananda.

166The mahanta Shyamananda, with supreme joy at heart,
went quickly to have darshan of Sri Gauranga.

167He saw the sweet form, streams flowed from his eyes,
and again and again he bowed, falling to the ground.

168All over his body a most lovely thrill;
his body was helpless in the ecstasy of prema.

169After a while, growing calm, he said to Sri Govinda:
"Let me have darshan of the five other Deities too."

170When Sri Govinda Kaviraja showed them to him,
what Shyamananda became I cannot describe.

171Where the provisions for the festival were kept,
he showed him that too, and seeing it he was greatly pleased.

172Meanwhile Sri Rasikananda, Sri Purushottama,
Sri Kishora and others, excellent in every way,

173had all the provisions they had brought from their land
placed in Gauranga's storeroom.

174The many people with them, by their care,
were given what was fitting and assigned lodgings.

175In this way Shyamananda's disciples, the life of the Vaishnavas,
arranged everything everywhere.

176Meanwhile Shyamananda went to where the Acharya was
and became absorbed in talks of Gaura and Krishna.

177Having passed that day in supreme bliss,
in the morning all performed their morning duties.

178Having bathed and so on, all thought within themselves:
"Why is Sri Jahnava Devi so late?"

179At that moment a brahmana carefully reported:
"Jahnava Ishvari has crossed the Padmavati."

180As soon as they heard it, all were filled with the bliss of prema
and went forward along the road to the bank of the Padmavati.

181People everywhere ran about, jostling;
all said, "Jahnava, full of prema, has come!"

182One of Sri Jahnava Ishvari's companions
came to announce the Ishvari's coming.

183Seeing the Acharya approach, with great joy at heart
he bowed to the ground and reported the Ishvari's coming.

184Acharya Mahashaya, bowing to him,
asked for particulars, and he related them in detail:

185"Receiving the news from here by letter,
all became eager to come here.

186There were the most generous Krishnadasa,
whose elder brother is Suryadasa Sarakhela,

187Shrila Raghupati Upadhyaya, Mahidhara,
Murari Chaitanya, the charming Jnanadasa,

188Kamalakara Piplai, Sri Jiva Pandita,
Madhava Acharya, whose deeds are well known,

189Nrisimha Chaitanya Dasa, Kanai, Shankara,
Sri Gauranga Dasa, the wise Vrindavana,

190Sri Minaketana Ramadasa Mahashaya,
Nakadi, Sri Balarama and others full of prema.

191All submitted at the feet of the two Ishvaris9
that they wished to go to Kheturi.

192Hearing this, Jahnava Ishvari said with delight:
'Why delay? Let us go there quickly.'

193At the Ishvari's command Sri Parameshvara Dasa
joyfully made everything ready for the journey.

194On the day the Ishvari set out from Khardaha,
Vaishnavas came from afar to see her.

195The Ishvari told them about the journey here,
and hearing it, all became eager.

196All went quickly to their homes and came back;
that is why there was delay, and they set out again.

197At the time of departure a voice spoke from the sky —
it was most wonderful; hear it, Mahashaya.

198In a deep and solemn voice it said again and again:
'Srinivasa and Narottama are dear to Me;

199with their people they are skilled in giving bhakti;
I am ever subdued by the prema of the two.

200In the village of Kheturi, in sankirtana with My associates,
I shall dance, and everyone will see it.

201By the power of My prema all people will be maddened;
no one will be left with any sorrow or grief.

202By your going there everything will be accomplished;
all are watching the road for you.

203From Kheturi you will go to Vrindavana,
and coming back from there you will distribute the treasure of bhakti.'

204Hearing this, the Ishvari was astonished at heart;
she could not be calm, tears flowed from her eyes.

205All the wise who were in the village of Khardaha,
and those who had come from other places —

206all, hearing it, were maddened with gladness of heart;
unable to check their tears, they were bathed in them.

207Sri Jahnava, remembering Gaura and Nityananda,
at once set out with everyone.

208Having told Sri Vasudha Devi something in private,
having carefully settled Ganga and Virachandra,

209having arranged everything in every way,
they travelled some distance by boat.

210As soon as they set out, the cry spread through the land:
"The Ishvari is going to Vraja by way of Kheturi."

211Some way along they left the boat
and went to the house of a fortunate, dear merchant.

212Day and night they are intoxicated with Nityananda's virtues;
at the sight of the Ishvari the bliss of prema surged up.

213Sri Ishvari, showing mercy to all,
stayed there that day with her people.

214Raghunatha, the son of lame Bhagavan,
the dearest disciple of Jagadisha Pandita,

215came and met the Ishvari there.
Rising very early, all came to Ambika.

216Sri Hridaya Chaitanya went out a long way
and brought the Ishvari and everyone to his house.

217What befell them at the sight of Nitai and Chaitanya-chand
cannot be described.

218After a while, regaining composure,
they ate and did their other duties there.

219Sri Jahnava Ishvari told Hridaya Chaitanya
everything, quietly.

220Hearing it, Sri Hridayananda rejoiced
and resolved to go to the village of Kheturi.

221Sri Vamshivadana's son Sri Chaitanya Dasa
at that moment came with his people to Prabhu.10

222Seeing the feet of Sri Jahnava Ishvari,
he deemed himself blessed; streams flowed from both his eyes.

223Again and again he bowed, falling to the ground,
and at the Ishvari's bidding grew calm and sat down.

224With gladness of heart they told him everything,
and hearing it he was overwhelmed with joy.

225Sri Chaitanya Dasa and others resolved:
'We shall go to Kheturi to see the holy festival.'

226With gladness of heart all made ready
and informed Sri Hridaya Chaitanya Thakura.

227From Shantipura came a man
who related the news from there:

228'Sri Achyutananda Prabhu, Advaita's son,
is so worn by separation that his life hangs in doubt.

229To carry out the command of Mother Sri Sita,
he will set out at dawn to go to Kheturi.'

230Hearing this, the Ishvari's joy grew greatly,
and she quickly sent all the news back by him.

231Sri Jahnava with everyone at the Pandita's house
passed the night with great gladness of heart.

232At dawn she saw the mangala-arati
and offered herself at the feet of Nitai and Chaitanya.

233Having bidden all engaged in the holy service to be careful,
the Ishvari set out with everyone for Navadvipa.

234Gazing from afar toward Sri Navadvipa,
she shed streams from both eyes that washed her breast.

235Remembering all those pastimes of Navadvipa,
she heaved sighs like tongues of flame.

236Her body grew helpless, her heart distraught;
after a while by Prabhu's will she grew calm.

237All those dear to Prabhu who were in Navadvipa
heard of Sri Jahnava Ishvari's coming.

238With gladness of heart all came forward to meet her;
seeing them from afar, the Ishvari got down from her palanquin.

239Having seen the Ishvari, all
extolled their own good fortune:

240'Today the Creator has given us a blessed morning!' —
saying this, they came near and bowed again and again.

241What Sri Jahnava Devi did, what was in her mind —
who understands the wondrous ways of prema?

242With the dear ones who had come with Sri Ishvari
all met, each as was fitting.

243At the meeting everyone's composure was gone:
some took the dust of another's feet again and again,

244some in prema, clasping one another by the neck,
remembering the Lord's pastimes, wept aloud.

245How wondrous is the glory of prema — who knows it?
After a while those dear to Prabhu grew calm.

246Srivasa Pandita's brother Pandita Shripati
said carefully to Sri Madhava Acharya and others:

247'It would be good to bathe in the Ganga here.'
Hearing these words, all were pleased.

248All bathed in the Ganga right there,
and Shripati hurried into Navadvipa,

249and quickly brought various provisions;
meanwhile all finished their bathing and daily rites.

250Sri Jahnava Ishvari, with supreme joy at heart,
fed everyone, having eaten a little herself.

251Quickly entering Navadvipa,
the Ishvari came to the house of Srivasa Pandita.

252There came the son of Prabhu Advaita,
named Sri Achyutananda, purifier of the worlds,

253Achyuta's brother Sri Gopala, full of prema,
Sri Kanu Pandita, Vishnudasa Mahashaya,

254Vanamali Dasa and other very wise ones —
their meeting was most wonderful.

255The ocean of prema surged immeasurably;
it cannot all be told with one mouth.

256Shrimati Ishvari, joyfully, in complete seclusion,
told everything to Sri Achyutananda.

257Hearing it, Prabhu Advaita's son, in prema,
lost all composure and roared incessantly.

258When Shripati, Shrinidhi and others were told,
all wished to see the festival.

259The news of the journey to Kheturi spread everywhere,
and all gathered at Srivasa's house.

260The bliss there was that day as all dined there
cannot be described.

261The people of Navadvipa ran from all sides;
there was a great crowd at Srivasa's house.

262Receiving the blessed sight of the Lord's associates,
they soothed hearts burned by the cruel fire of sorrow.

263After part of the night all the people went home,
and the Lord's associates all lay down to sleep.

264Rising at dawn, all set out quickly
and came to Akaihat, to Krishnadasa's house.

265The excellent singer Krishnadasa, in prema,
bringing them to his home, deemed himself blessed.

266Preparing food very quickly,
he made ready to go to Kheturi.

267Rising at dawn, all with joyful hearts
came very quickly to Kantaka-nagara.

268First Krishnadasa Thakura went
and told Sri Yadunandana everything in detail.

269As soon as he heard it, with great gladness of heart
he went forward and quickly brought them to his house.

270There came Sri Raghunandana with his people;
with Shivananda came the brahmana Vaninatha,

271Vallabha, Chaitanya Dasa, Bhagavata Acharya,
the dancer Gopala, the best of brahmanas Jita Mishra,

272Raghu Mishra, Kashinatha, Pandita Uddhava,
Sri Nayanananda Mishra, Mangala Vaishnava —

273so came many dear to Prabhu,
and their meeting was most wonderful.

274Seeing the beauty of Dasa Gadadhara's Gauranga,
all were enraptured, and their eyes were soothed.

275To where Gaurachandra took sannyasa
all went, weeping and weeping.

276The state they all fell into at the mere sight of the place —
all that cannot come from my mouth.

277After a while all grew calm
and quickly bathed in the Ganga.

278Meanwhile Yadunandana and others, with great care,
arranged various sweets on plates,

279offered them row on row to Sri Gaurachandra
and placed them separately in the lodgings.

280All meanwhile finished their bathing and other rites
and partook of Sri maha-prasada with great care.

281That day Jahnava Ishvari herself,
with joy in her heart, went quickly to the kitchen

282and quickly cooked many kinds of dishes;
hearing of it, all were astonished.

283She offered the food to Sri Gaurangachandra,
and Prabhu ate in supreme bliss.

284After a while she carefully removed the offering
and with the greatest care fed everyone.

285Everything was like nectar — what comparison can be given?
Whoever ate forgot himself in bliss.

286Sri Ishvari partook of the prasada,
and the minds of all the mahantas rejoiced.

287Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti and all the rest
ate afterwards, with all care.

288What they felt as they tasted the Sri maha-prasada
cannot be told: streams flowed from both their eyes.

289Remembering his own beloved Dasa Gadadhara,
he grew calm after a while, sitting in seclusion.

290Greatly eager to go to Kheturi,
he made preparations for going there.

291The servants who serve Sri Gaurachandra
he instructed to be careful in every way.

292When everything was done, evening came,
and all the mahantas came to Gauranga's courtyard.

293Having seen the arati of Sri Gaurachandra,
they sang the holy name for a while.

294All passed the night in the relish of talks about Krishna
and slept a little, with gladness of heart.

295At dawn, bowing to Gaurachandra,
they all came along the road this way, addressing everyone.

296Today they quickly crossed the Padmavati
and sent me to bring you the news at once."

297Hearing all this, Acharya Thakura
became such as words cannot express.

298In the hearts of Sri Thakura Mahashaya, Shyamananda and the others
joy reached its limit.

299As they went, they saw before their eyes
everyone coming, radiant as the sun.

300As they gazed, their eyes forgot to blink;
their bodies grew helpless; they could not walk.

301Seeing their state, Jahnava Ishvari,
remembering Prabhu, got down from her palanquin.

302Sri Achyuta and others who were in carriages
gladly and quickly got down to the ground.

303Srinivasa Acharya and others, awash in tears of prema,
fell rolling at the Ishvari's feet.

304Sri Jahnava Ishvari could not be calm;
the mercy she showed — who could tell it?

305To Sri Achyutananda and the others dear to Prabhu
they bowed at the feet one by one.

306Gazing at Srinivasa Acharya and the others,
Sri Achyutananda and the rest could not restrain their hearts.

307One, embracing Srinivasa, wept;
one embraced Narottama again and again;

308one, embracing Ramachandra, would not let him go;
one drenched Sri Gokulananda with tears;

309one, spreading his arms, clasped Shridasa;
one showed great affection to Shyamananda;

310one, gazing at Sri Govinda Kaviraja's face,
embraced him, and streams from his eyes washed his breast.

311Seeing such ways of prema, such a wondrous meeting,
even the gods deemed themselves blessed.

312As they entered the village, people ran from all sides;
the village of Kheturi was drowned in a flood of bliss.

313Acharya Thakura, respectfully asking everyone's leave,
took them to separate lodgings.

314Where the Ishvari's lodging with her people was,
there he appointed Ramachandra Kaviraja.

315To the lodging of Raghunatha Acharya and others
he appointed Kaviraja Karnapura.

316Where Hridaya Chaitanya's lodging was,
there he carefully appointed Shyamananda.

317Where Sri Chaitanya Dasa and others put up,
there he appointed Sri Nrisimha Kaviraja.

318To the lodging of Shripati, Shrinidhi Pandita and others
he appointed Sri Vyasa Acharya.

319To the lodging of Krishnadasa of Akaihat and others
Sri Vallavikanta was appointed.

320In the lodging where Sri Raghunandana was with his people,
Sri Govinda Kaviraja was appointed.

321To the house of the brahmana Vaninatha, Jita Mishra and others
he appointed Rama, Krishna, Kumuda and others.

322To Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti's lodging
he carefully appointed Kaviraja Bhagavan.

323Where the lodgings of other Vaishnavas were,
there he appointed Sri Gopiramana and others.

324Going everywhere and arranging everything,
he gave each a separate storeroom.

325There were so many provisions there that they cannot be counted,
ever full by the will of Krishna Chaitanya.

326Sri Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya
went about everywhere again and again in prema.

327Such is the coming of the mahantas to the village of Sri Kheturi;
whoever hears of it has his desires fulfilled.

328Listen to all this continually and with care:
Narahari tells the Narottama-vilasa.

Thus ends the sixth vilasa of the Narottama-vilasa.

Notes

  1. "The Moon of Navadvipa with His Beloved": the Deity of Gauranga with Vishnupriya (cf. v. 56).
  2. A verse from Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Stavamrita-lahari (his octet on Narottama).
  3. The Deity of Gauranga with His two consorts, Lakshmipriya and Vishnupriya.
  4. That is, five other Deities, whom Narottama would install in Kheturi together with Gauranga (Vilasa 7).
  5. Srinivasa Acharya.
  6. Ramachandra was the son of Chiranjiva Sena and, through his mother, grandson of the poet Damodara Sena; cf. BR.
  7. Devidasa, Gokula and Gauranga (Dasa), disciples of Narottama, singers and musicians of his kirtana.
  8. Disciples of Srinivasa.
  9. Vasudha and Jahnava, the consorts of Nityananda.
  10. "Prabhu": the Deities of Gaura-Nitai at Ambika (or Hridaya Chaitanya); Chaitanya Dasa is the son of Vamshivadana.
